title: Faraday's law

draft.title: Faraday's law
card: An emf is induced in a circuit when the magnetic flux through it changes. If the flux stays constant, no emf is induced.
Faraday's law says the induced emf equals the rate of change of flux, for a coil of N turns: emf = -N × ΔΦ/Δt.
The faster the flux changes, the bigger the emf. A coil with more turns gives a bigger emf for the same change in flux.
Flux can change if the field strength changes, if the area changes, or if the angle between the field and the area changes.
draft.remember: No change in flux, no emf. A faster change gives a bigger emf.

a.q: A magnet is held still inside a coil of wire. Why is no emf induced in the coil?
opts: The magnetic flux through the coil is not changing
The magnetic flux through the coil is zero
The magnet is too weak to produce any flux
The coil has no turns of wire in the field
a.why: An emf needs a changing flux, and a still magnet gives a steady flux. The flux is not zero, so a strong field alone is not enough to induce an emf.
a.clue: What must the flux be doing for an emf to appear?

b.q: A coil of 100 turns has the flux through it fall from 0.050 Wb to 0.020 Wb in 0.10 s. What is the size of the average induced emf?
b.why: Change in flux = 0.030 Wb. emf = N × ΔΦ/Δt = 100 × 0.030 ÷ 0.10 = 30 V. Leaving out the number of turns gives 0.30 V, which is the tempting mistake.
b.clue: Multiply the rate of change of flux by the number of turns.

a.best: The magnetic flux through the coil is not changing
